evidence: The report creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md, lines 1635-1649, places c842 in "Randomized experiments under 50 participants". Line 1637 explicitly says these studies are omitted from the dataset "whatever their outcome" and acknowledges the unresolved output criterion. creativity-codebook.md, Section 3, lines 30-34, requires all three criteria for entry into the core dataset; line 44 separately lists randomized experiments with fewer than 50 participants among works retained in the screening report and omitted from the dataset. It does not require criterion 3 to be met for that descriptive category. I opened the PDF named by retrieval.json[c842], C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Liu et al (2024) - How AI Processing Delays Foster Creativity.pdf, with PyMuPDF: p. 8, Section 6, reports 20 HCI researchers; p. 9, Section 6.1, states that condition/topic orders and combinations were randomly assigned, and Section 7.1.1 again reports 20 participants. The outcome uncertainty is supported by p. 6, Section 5.1.2 (AI generates three questions per turn), p. 9, Sections 6.2.1 and 6.2.3 (participants rate at least six generated questions and logs count generated questions), and p. 22, Table 3 (the creativity survey includes how creative participants felt). forms/c842.json correctly retains core=no, criterion_1=met, criterion_2=not_met, and criterion_3=unclear; forms/checks/c842.json preserves that uncertainty. tools/build_report.py, lines 145-149, explicitly permits small when criterion 3 is unclear, and tools/assemble_report.py, lines 179-183, discloses that uncertainty in the section introduction. The finding adds an output-eligibility requirement for small that the cited codebook does not impose. The classification is supported; no correction is warranted.
